name: Linux Server Hunt
author: Infrastructure Security
prerequisites: Auditd installed and collecting on all targets
Root or sudo privilege for artifact collection
SSH key-based access to target systems

hunt_actions.title: Unauthorized Account and Privilege Escalation
actions: Review /etc/passwd for unexpected accounts: `awk -F: '$3 >= 1000 && $7 != "/sbin/nologin" && $7 != "/bin/false" {print $1, $3, $6, $7}' /etc/passwd` — compare output against approved user list; any unknown UID >= 1000 with a valid shell warrants investigation.

Detect SUID/SGID binaries added outside package manager: `find / -xdev \( -perm -4000 -o -perm -2000 \) -type f -print0 2>/dev/null | xargs -0 ls -la | sort` — compare against a known-good baseline: `rpm -Va --nodigest 2>/dev/null | grep '^.M'` (RPM) or `dpkg --verify 2>/dev/null | grep 'not installed\|MD5 mismatch'` (Debian).

Hunt for sudo rule modifications: `find /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d/ -newer /var/log/apt/history.log -ls 2>/dev/null` and `aureport --auth -ts today` — review any rule granting NOPASSWD or ALL=(ALL) to non-standard accounts. Also check: `visudo -c` for syntax errors that may indicate injection.

Identify SSH authorized_keys additions: `find /root /home -name authorized_keys -newer /etc/passwd -ls 2>/dev/null` and `ausearch -k auth -ts today | grep authorized_keys` — each new key entry should correspond to an approved provisioning event.

hunt_actions.title: Persistence via Cron and Services
actions: Audit all cron jobs across system and user crontabs: `for f in /etc/cron.d/* /etc/cron.daily/* /etc/cron.hourly/* /etc/cron.weekly/* /etc/cron.monthly/*; do echo "=== $f ==="; cat $f 2>/dev/null; done` and `for u in $(cut -f1 -d: /etc/passwd); do echo "=== $u ==="; crontab -l -u $u 2>/dev/null; done` — any script referencing /tmp, /dev/shm, or curl/wget is suspicious.

Detect systemd units added outside package management: `find /etc/systemd/system /usr/local/lib/systemd /run/systemd/system -name '*.service' -newer /usr/lib/systemd -ls 2>/dev/null` — inspect suspicious unit files with `systemctl cat <unit>` and verify the ExecStart binary is signed and expected.

Review /etc/rc.local and init.d for unauthorized scripts: `cat /etc/rc.local 2>/dev/null; ls -la /etc/init.d/ | sort -k6,7` — compare init.d modification dates against known deployment dates. Any recently modified init script must be reviewed line-by-line.

Hunt for LD_PRELOAD abuse: `grep -r 'LD_PRELOAD\|LD_LIBRARY_PATH' /etc/environment /etc/profile /etc/profile.d/ /etc/ld.so.preload /home/*/.bashrc /home/*/.bash_profile /root/.bashrc 2>/dev/null` — LD_PRELOAD pointing to an unknown .so file indicates potential rootkit or hijacking.

hunt_actions.title: Log Tampering and Defense Evasion
actions: Identify gaps or deletions in auth logs: `ausearch -m USER_LOGIN -ts $(date -d '30 days ago' +%m/%d/%Y) | grep -c 'type=USER_LOGIN'` then compare count against expected baseline. Also: `find /var/log -name 'auth.log*' -o -name 'secure*' | xargs ls -lh` — look for zero-byte log files or unexpected gaps in inode modification time.

Detect shell history clearing: `ausearch -k historian -ts today 2>/dev/null` (if auditd watches history files) or `find /home /root -name '.bash_history' -empty -o -name '.bash_history' -newer /etc/passwd | xargs ls -lh 2>/dev/null` — also check for `HISTFILE=/dev/null` or `unset HISTFILE` in shell rc files.

Hunt for use of shred, wipe, dd, or truncate on log files: `ausearch -x shred -ts today 2>/dev/null; ausearch -x wipe -ts today 2>/dev/null; grep -r 'truncate\|shred\|dd if=/dev/null' /var/log/syslog /var/log/messages 2>/dev/null` — also examine: `ausearch -f /var/log -ts today | grep -E 'UNLINK|RENAME'` for log file deletions.

questions: Is auditd installed, actively running, and configured with a hardened ruleset (e.g., STIG or CIS Level 2 audit rules) on all in-scope Linux systems?
Are auditd logs forwarded in real time to a central SIEM, and what is the maximum acceptable log forwarding lag before an alert is triggered?
Are all in-scope servers enrolled in a configuration management system (Ansible, Puppet, Chef, or Salt), and can the system generate a diff against the last known-good configuration state?
Is SSH hardened on all systems to prohibit root login (PermitRootLogin no), enforce public key authentication only (PasswordAuthentication no), and use a non-standard port or port knocking?
Is an endpoint telemetry agent (OSQuery, Velociraptor, or equivalent) deployed and actively collecting process, network, file integrity, and user session data?
Are file integrity monitoring (FIM) tools (AIDE, Tripwire, or Wazuh FIM) deployed and running on schedule, with baseline databases stored offline or read-only?
Is there a documented and approved list of expected cron jobs, systemd timers, and services for each server role, against which deviations can be measured?
Are privileged accounts (root, service accounts with sudo) managed through a Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution (e.g., CyberArk, HashiCorp Vault) with session recording?
